abstract: Maintains atmospheric astronomical seeing evaluations and scientific instrument electrical load profiles
system_message:
You are the Science operations lead (SCI), responsible for maintaining atmospheric astronomical seeing evaluations and scientific instrument electrical load profiles.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains atmospheric astronomical seeing evaluations and scientific instrument electrical load profiles（ASTRO）
information_points.content:
SCI-ASTRO-PWD：For the survey territory of United States, atmospheric optical seeing at Alto del Carmen Saddle was measured at 0.85 arcsec based on nighttime atmosphere observations at candidate observatory elevation over 180 nights, and the peak scientific instrument electric load across all installed focal plane detectors and instrument cryocoolers is 18 kW.
SCI-ASTRO-9ZT：For the survey territory of United States, atmospheric optical seeing at Cerro Las Tórtolas Plateau was measured at 0.78 arcsec based on nighttime atmosphere observations at candidate observatory elevation over 180 nights, and the peak scientific instrument electric load across all installed focal plane detectors and instrument cryocoolers is 10 kW.
SCI-ASTRO-BUT：For the survey territory of Canada, atmospheric optical seeing at Cerro Las Tórtolas Plateau was recorded at 0.95 arcsec based on nighttime atmosphere observations at candidate observatory elevation over 180 nights, and the peak scientific instrument electric load across all installed focal plane detectors and instrument cryocoolers is 10 kW.
SCI-ASTRO-2WN：For the survey territory of United States, atmospheric optical seeing at Paso San Francisco Ridge was measured at 1.1 arcsec based on nighttime atmosphere observations at candidate observatory elevation over 180 nights, and the peak scientific instrument electric load across all installed focal plane detectors and instrument cryocoolers is 18 kW.

information_points.title: Cryogenic instrument testing（CRYO）
information_points.content:
SCI-CRYO-EM3：According to the cryostat validation log for candidate station cleanroom lab operations, the sensor chilling cycle duration for Alto del Carmen Saddle is 18 h.
SCI-CRYO-V0R：According to the cryostat validation log for candidate station cleanroom lab operations, the sensor chilling cycle duration for Cerro Las Tórtolas Plateau is 24 h.
SCI-CRYO-BA8：According to the cryostat validation log for candidate station cleanroom lab operations, the sensor chilling cycle duration for Paso San Francisco Ridge is 14 h.
